english: What are you weaving, mother? I weave a garment for your brother. Go and sit with me at the loom. Show me the threads. Which threads are straight? Lead the white thread through them. I lead the thread. Daughter, you have learned. When you have grown up you will weave your own garments. Teach me again early (tomorrow). At dawn go, and we weave.

english: Son, the sheep have come home; one lamb has been left behind. Mother, I saw it in the field. Where did the lamb go? Look for it near the river before night comes. I take the dog with me. The dog smells out lambs. Now, are you afraid of the night? I am not afraid; it (the dog) is with me.

Shepherd, it is getting dark; where is our home (camp)? Look up at the stars. One bright star stands above our home. We will walk toward it. Hold my hand and don't fall. Who showed you the stars? An old woman showed them to me when I was small. Now I show them to you. Will you remember them? I will remember them.

english: Grandmother, the fire on the hearth has become small. What shall I do? Lay dry wood on the coals and it will grow. Now smoke goes up and the fire burns. The fire must not die in our house. Our grandfathers kept it. Why do we guard it? Fire is a god; it warms the house. Will you guard it at night? I will guard it and not sleep.

english: Boy, are you sitting on the horse's back? I am not sitting; I am afraid of horses. Don't be afraid. I myself tamed the foal. Take hold of its mane and hold on. I am holding. Grip it with your two knees and look forward. Now I am riding. Do you see me? I see you. Soon you will ride swift horses.

english: Child, can you swim? I don't swim; the river is deep. Climb onto my back and I will carry you. Now move your arms and legs. I am swimming; are you holding me? I am not holding you; you swim by yourself. Will you be used to it soon? We'll be used to it, and laugh.
